items.content_html:
Description

Expands the IDBDatabase: versionchange event page to explain why the event matters: an upgrade or deletion requested from another connection waits until every other connection is closed, closing the connection in the versionchange handler is the usual way to let it proceed, and the requesting side gets a blocked event while connections remain open. Replaces the examples with one that closes the connection in onversionchange and one that handles blocked on the requesting side. The one-line summary on the IDBDatabase page now says the handler should close the database.

Motivation

#26639 points out that the page barely explains versionchange, even though not handling it leaves another tab's upgrade stuck.

Additional details

Validation boundary: the behavior described follows the "open a database connection" / "delete a database" steps of the IndexedDB spec (fire versionchange at other connections, fire blocked if any remain open, wait for them to close) and the existing "Version changes while a web app is open in another tab" section, which the page now links to. I removed claims from an earlier draft about stale tabs silently corrupting data, because I could not source them. I did not run the examples in a browser or build the site locally.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #26639

AI assistance disclosure: this change was prepared with the help of an AI coding agent (Grok Bot) and has not been reviewed line by line by the account owner.

items.content_html:
Description

Removes the "Firefox default-src: none SVG sprite blocking issue" section from the default-src CSP reference page.

Motivation

That section documented a Firefox-only workaround for external SVG sprites (<use href="file.svg#id">) being blocked under default-src 'none'; img-src 'self'. Firefox fixed this in version 132 (bug 1773976, RESOLVED FIXED, status-firefox132: fixed), and the page already carries a note saying so. The Firefox engineer who landed the fix noted in comment 15 that #34592 "should probably be mostly reverted" afterwards.

Additional details

#34592 also touched content-security-policy/index.md and the CSP practical implementation guide; those parts no longer contain the Firefox SVG sprite text on main, so only this section remained. I searched mdn/content for links to the removed section's anchor and found none. Docs-only; I did not run the local build.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #36745
Relates to #34592

Description

Adds a note to HTMLImageElement.decode() about images with loading="lazy" that have not loaded yet: Firefox rejects the returned promise with an EncodingError DOMException while Chrome does not, and calling decode() from an onload handler works in both.

Motivation

The page says decode() "can be used to initiate loading of the image", which is misleading for lazy-loaded images that haven't loaded, and readers hit an unexplained EncodingError: Invalid image request. in Firefox.

Additional details

Behavior as reported in the issue and in https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65146920/domexception-invalid-image-request. I did not run a browser test myself; the note only states the reported Firefox/Chrome difference and the onload workaround the reporter confirmed.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #38034

items.content_html:
Description

The previous human vocal range numbers are unreasonable and did not have sources. This PR takes the numbers from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice_frequency .

Motivation

Most businesswomen and all men do not reach 300 Hz much less 500 Hz during normal non-singing talking.

Additional details

  • Asserting human 300 Hz lower bound -> include male 90 Hz lower bound
  • Clarify it's "harmonic series a.k.a." overtones, following the #Fundamental_frequency section, not just a vague "the waveform"
  • Use the narrowband 3,400 Hz not 3 kHz upper limit for "telephone networks"
  • Replace the unsourced 500 Hz to 3 kHz range with 300 Hz to 3.4 kHz from a .gov website

I did not touch the 18 kHz upper bounds despite my sibilants and plosives sounding fine when beyond 10 kHz is cut off. I also will not challenge the 300 Hz lower bound despite the "y" vowel F1 formant requiring 235 Hz.

Related issues and pull requests

N/A

items.content_html:
Description

Adds a paragraph to "Focusable elements should have interactive semantics" on the Keyboard accessible guide: in browse mode, some screen readers intercept Enter and Space and activate the element with a click event, so keydown and keyup handlers never run. Touch screen readers fire click on double tap. The paragraph tells readers to handle click as well, or use a native <button>. Also adds the click event to the section's "See also" list and fixes "event handlers keyboard events" to "event handlers for keyboard events".

Motivation

The section only recommends keyboard event handlers. A custom control built that way does nothing for an NVDA user in browse mode, which is the case reported in the issue.

Additional details

  • NVDA discussion of the behavior: nvaccess/nvda#7898
  • Checked in Chromium: a focused <button> fires click on both Enter and Space; a focused <div tabindex="0"> gets only keydown and keyup.
  • markdownlint-cli2 and prettier -c pass on the file.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #37887
items.title: Keyboard accessible: note that screen readers can replace key events with click
